correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the 31-point quadratic-residue tournament and enumerated every transitive subtournament, giving f=(31,465,3255,9765,10695,3255,465), 27931 nonempty simplices. Independently recomputed complete mod-two simplicial boundary ranks (30,435,2820,6945,2790,465), hence mod-two Betti (1,0,0,0,960,0,0); Euler characteristic forces rational H4 dimension960 and rational vanishing elsewhere. Each orientation-preserving affine symmetry fixes a transitive face setwise only when it fixes every vertex (unique compatible order), so Lefschetz gives 960 identity, -1 for 30 nontrivial translations, 0 for remaining 434 elements; exactly 2Q[G]⊕Q[F31]/Q·1. Restriction to translations gives cyclotomic rational irreducibility and fixed ranks 2 globally/30 under C31. Does not infer torsion-free integral homology or full tournament automorphism classification.

value.rationale: The 31-point Paley tournament is a canonical highly symmetric doubly regular tournament beyond the earlier finite census. Identifying its 960-dimensional top homology with 2 regular plus vertex augmentation gives a complete natural affine representation, rational invariant dimensions 2/30 and distinction from the known bare wedge type. A natural exact finite equivariant classification can be intrinsically useful without an infinite-family theorem.

limitations: The theorem is rational and for the specified order-465 affine subgroup, not the full automorphism group by classification.
Full text of Deniz 2014 unavailable due Oxford VPN disconnect; named residual risk.
The independent finite boundary reduction does not establish integral torsion-freeness.
